title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Derwin James Jr. (hamstring) won't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Derwin James Jr. (hamstring) won't take part in Los Angeles' practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran safety is not going to practice on Wednesday. He missed last week's game due to a hamstring issue, and he's at risk of missing another game in Week 6 for the same reason. Los Angeles' defense will be weaker than usual ahead of a tough matchup against the Chiefs if they are without their veteran safety.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kayode Awosika (leg) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Kayode Awosika (leg) is missing Los Angeles' practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: A leg injury is going to leave Awosika sidelined for the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday. He seems likely to miss another game with this injury, but we won't get an official injury designation for him until later on in the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Joe Alt (neck) not practicing Wednesday
items.desc: Joe Alt (neck) is not taking part in practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: To no surprise, Alt is not practicing for the Chargers on Wednesday. He's dealing with a neck injury and is seeing a specialist because of it, which makes it seem highly unlikely that he will play in Week 6. Los Angeles' offense will continue to be weaker than usual until he's back in the lineup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ladd McConkey (foot) expected to practice Wednesday
items.desc: Ladd McConkey (foot) is expected to take part in Los Angeles' practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: McConkey didn't see any action in last week's game due to a foot issue, but he is expected to make his return to practice on Wednesday. He will likely be limited, but we won't know for sure until sometime after practice. He will be hard to start in Week 6 against a tough Chiefs' defense considering how bad Los Angeles' offense has been throughout the start of the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) officially doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Lamar Jackson (ankle) officially did not take part in Baltimore's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Jackson was a non-participant at practice to start the week on Wednesday. He's still recovering from an ankle injury that left him sidelined last week, and it may very well leave him sidelined for another game in Week 6. Tyler Huntley will get another start for the Ravens if that's the case, but we won't know for sure until later on in the week.

items.impact: Mayfield is likely to miss another game this week as he continues to work his way back from a thumb injury. He remains week-to-week.

items.impact: Odeyingbo will miss at least one game. He will not be placed on injured reserve.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Zach Charbonnet (knee) has 'legitimate chance' to return in Week 7
items.desc: Zach Charbonnet has a "legitimate chance" to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
items.impact: This was the expectation with the Seahawks having a mini bye following the team playing on Thursday this week. He'll likely be eased back, but the Seahawks need him back more than ever right now given the struggles with the run game.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Tyreek Hill remains in talks with multiple teams
items.desc: Tyreek Hill's agent Drew Rosenhaus said he remains in talks with multiple NFL teams.
items.impact: Hill continues to rehab his surgically repaired knee. Rosenhaus added that "nothing is imminent at this time." He remains without a clear timetable to sign and return.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Ashton Jeanty 'feeling a lot better physically' per Klint Kubiak
items.desc: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty is starting to "feel a lot better" physically.
items.impact: There had been rumors of the Raiders potentially having Jeanty sit a week to get fully healthy. When asked if the team considered sitting Jeanty to get him healthy, Kubiak said, "he's playing."
